items.followUp: What is crossing over, and what are the points where chromatids cross called?

rubric.why: Identifies which chromatids take part in crossing over.
rubric.description: States that crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the non-sister chromatids and their homologous chromosomes.

rubric.why: Describes the exchange that defines crossing over.
rubric.description: Explains that the chromatids exchange corresponding segments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the exchange of corresponding segments.

modelAnswer: During prophase I of meiosis, non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes exchange corresponding segments; this is called crossing over.
The points where the chromatids cross and remain attached are called chiasmata.

items.followUp: Differentiate between autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition.

rubric.why: Defines nutrients as substances required by organisms.
rubric.description: States that nutrients are substances needed for energy, growth or repair.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition of nutrients.

rubric.why: Defines nutrition as a process involving nutrients.
rubric.description: States that nutrition is the process by which an organism obtains and uses nutrients.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining nutrition as a process of obtaining or using nutrients.

modelAnswer: Nutrients are substances required by an organism for energy, growth, repair and other life processes.
Nutrition is the process by which an organism obtains and utilizes nutrients.

items.followUp: What are micronutrients? Give one example required by plants.

rubric.why: States the defining feature of macronutrients.
rubric.description: Defines macronutrients as nutrients required by plants in large amounts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that plants require macronutrients in large amounts or quantities.

rubric.why: Gives a valid example of a plant macronutrient.
rubric.description: Gives an example such as nitrogen, phosphorus or potassium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming any valid plant macronutrient.

modelAnswer: Macronutrients are nutrients required by plants in large amounts.
Examples include nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.
